Journal of Virology.title: Epstein-Barr virus BMRF1 recruits NuRD to replicating viral DNA to facilitate viral genome amplification.
Journal of Virology.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Epstein-Barr virus genomes are maintained as chromatinized episomes in latent infection but, upon reactivation to the lytic cycle, these genomes are amplified to produce linear products lacking histones. BMRF1 plays an essential role in EBV genome amplification as the DNA polymerase processivity factor and contains an additional domain that can transactivate gene expression through interaction with the cellular chromatin remodeling complex, NuRD. Here, we investigate the role of NuRD in EBV infection. Through silencing NuRD subunits, we found that CHD4, but not other NuRD subunits, suppressed EBV reactivation, while multiple NuRD subunits contributed to lytic DNA amplification. We generated EBV BACmids and virus with a BMRF1 mutation that disrupts NuRD binding and compared their lytic infection to that of WT EBV. The BMRF1 mutation decreased viral genome amplification without significant effects on immediate early or early gene expression. Additionally, while NuRD subunits localize to replicating WT EBV genomes, this association was greatly reduced by the BMRF1 mutation that disrupts NuRD binding. The data indicate that BMRF1 recruits NuRD to lytically replicating EBV, where it facilitates EBV genome amplification, likely through chromatin remodeling. [IMPORTANCE] The Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) BMRF1 protein plays an essential role in the synthesis of EBV genomes that are used to generate infectious virus by enabling replication by the viral DNA polymerase. In addition to this function, we have found that BMRF1 binds the cellular nucleosome remodeling complex called NuRD. We investigated the role of NuRD components in EBV genome synthesis, as well as the impact of a mutation in EBV that disrupts the BMRF1-NuRD interaction. The results indicate that NuRD components and the BMRF1-NuRD interaction are important for efficient EBV genome replication. We further showed that BMRF1 recruits NuRD to replicating EBV DNA, where it likely facilitates EBV replication through chromatin remodeling. Thus, we have identified a new role for BMRF1 and NuRD in EBV DNA replication.

Journal of Virology.title: Engineering BHK-21 cells by dual knockout of host-restriction factors Cav1 and HDAC6 achieved a marked increase in FMDV titers for scalable vaccine production.
Journal of Virology.abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) vaccine production depends on BHK-21 cells, but the high antigen dose required for biannual mass vaccination campaigns using an inactivated vaccine limits global vaccine supply. In this study, a targeted small-molecule screen identified baicalein (caveolin-1 inhibitor) and tubacin (HDAC6 inhibitor) as potent enhancers of FMDV replication in BHK-21 cells. Cav1 was shown to act as an early restriction factor: its inhibition increased the viral entry and consequently produced a sixfold higher virus yield. Cav1 inhibition also primed p53-dependent intrinsic apoptosis, raising p53 phosphorylation and BAX/BIM transcripts, shifting cells into early apoptosis, and promoting cytolytic spread. HDAC6 was shown to function as a post-entry restriction factor: its inhibition elevated α-tubulin acetylation, enhancing viral RNA and protein expression and producing four to six times titer boost. Finally, using CRISPR/Cas9, we generated Cav1/HDAC6 double-knockout (dKO) BHK-21 cells, targeting two host restriction factors that impose entry and post-entry barriers to FMDV replication. The engineered BHK-21 cells in both adherent and suspension culture formats produced 10- to 20-fold higher virus titers across field FMDV serotype "O" and FMDV vaccine strains of serotypes "O," "A," and "Asia 1." Reintroducing either factor restored restriction, confirming their roles as host restriction factors. These findings reveal a dual-layer host defense mechanism and establish an engineered, high-yield BHK-21 cell line for enhanced viral production and improved vaccine manufacturing efficiency.IMPORTANCEFoot-and-mouth disease (FMD) imposes substantial economic losses on livestock-producing countries through reduced animal productivity and trade restrictions. Control relies on biannual herd vaccination, generating a demand for vaccine that often exceeds current manufacturing capacity. FMD vaccine antigen is conventionally produced in BHK-21 cells; however, limited viral yields increase production costs and constrain supply. Here, we identify caveolin-1 and HDAC6 as host restriction factors for foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) in BHK-21 cells. Caveolin-1 restricts FMDV at the entry stage, whereas HDAC6 acts at a post-entry step. Knockout of these factors enhances viral yields by 10- to 20-fold across FMDV serotypes O, A, and Asia 1-the three serotypes included in India's trivalent vaccine program. These findings indicate that BHK-21 cells deficient in caveolin-1 and HDAC6 could substantially improve FMDV propagation and provide a scalable, cost-effective platform for vaccine manufacturing.

Journal of Virology.title: Extracellular vesicles enable rotavirus and astrovirus infection of low-susceptibility cell lines.
Journal of Virology.abstract: Rotaviruses (RVA) and human astroviruses (HAstV) are classical gastrointestinal pathogens, but increasing evidence indicates that they are also involved in a range of extraintestinal diseases. These include seizures and diabetes in RVA infections, and central nervous system infections in HAstV infections. However, the mechanisms by which these viruses disseminate beyond the intestine remain unclear. Given the previously described association of RVA and HAstV with extracellular vesicles (EVs), we investigated whether purified EV-virus complexes could mediate infection of cells with low susceptibility to these viruses. We found that the RVA strain RRV, as well as two HAstV strains (the classical HAstV-8, Yuc8 strain, and the divergent non-classical VA1 strain), could infect low-susceptibility cell lines (BHK, SK-N-SH, F11, and CHO) when associated with EVs. This infectivity was dependent on EV integrity, since disruption of vesicles by detergent treatment reduced infection. Furthermore, a fraction of viral particles was protected from neutralizing antibodies, most likely because they were enclosed within EVs. Together, these findings suggest that EVs may act as vehicles facilitating the dissemination of RVA and HAstV beyond the gastrointestinal tract.IMPORTANCEGastrointestinal viruses typically infect specific intestinal cell types; however, rotaviruses (RVA) and human astroviruses (HAstV) have been associated with a range of extraintestinal pathologies. To better understand how these viruses disseminate beyond the intestine, we investigated the potential role of their interactions with extracellular vesicles (EVs). We found that the simian RVA strain RRV and HAstV strains Yuc8 and VA1, when associated with EVs, could infect low-susceptibility cells. A fraction of the EV-associated viral particles was resistant to antibody-mediated neutralization, suggesting that EVs protected them. These observations support the possibility that EVs could serve as vehicles enabling RVA and HAstV to disseminate beyond the gastrointestinal tract.

Journal of Virology.title: The β-ladder domain of TMUV NS1 enhances viral replication in avian cells by modulating its interaction with the NS4A-2K-NS4B complex.
Journal of Virology.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Tembusu virus (TMUV), a mosquito‑borne flavivirus, represents a major threat to waterfowl farming in East and Southeast Asia. In vivo studies have noted distinct viral loads and viremia between ducklings infected with mosquito‑derived TMUV (mTMUV) and duck‑derived TMUV (dTMUV), yet the viral elements driving such phenotypic divergence remain unknown. The multifunctional nonstructural glycoprotein NS1 participates in flavivirus replication, secretion, and immune regulation. Here, we generated a panel of chimeric TMUV viruses with full‑length NS1 exchanges and NS1 domain substitutions based on mTMUV and dTMUV backbones. Our results demonstrated that NS1 modulates TMUV phenotypes in a strain-, dose-, and genetic background-dependent manner. Subcutaneous inoculation mimicking natural mosquito transmission amplified inter‑group phenotypic discrepancies, verifying NS1 as a pivotal modulator of TMUV‑triggered viremia. Since duck peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) infection underpins in vivo local viral establishment, an in vitro PBMC infection model validated the key contributory roles of NS1 and its functional domains in sustaining viral infection. We further utilized duck embryo fibroblasts (DEFs) to dissect the function of candidate NS1 domains. Domain swapping identified the β‑ladder domain as a major contributor to enhanced viral replication. Mechanistically, this replication enhancement effect correlates with strengthened interaction between NS1 and the NS4A-2K-NS4B replication complex. Collectively, our results identify the NS1 β-ladder domain as a critical determinant for TMUV infection. By modulating the interaction between NS1 and the NS4A-2K-NS4B complex, this domain regulates viral RNA replication efficiency in different hosts and consequently modulates viral dissemination and pathogenicity of TMUV. [IMPORTANCE] Tembusu virus (TMUV) severely threatens waterfowl production across East and Southeast Asia. Noticeable phenotypic differences exist between mosquito-derived and duck-derived TMUV; however, the viral determinants responsible for this variation remain poorly understood. Although flavivirus NS1 is a multifunctional glycoprotein, how it mediates TMUV host-specific phenotypes remains incompletely characterized. Using chimeric and mutant viruses, this study demonstrates that the NS1 β-ladder domain enhances viral replication by strengthening the interaction with the NS4A-2K-NS4B replication complex. This domain governs TMUV replication efficiency across hosts, thereby controlling viral dissemination and pathogenicity. Our findings uncover a key molecular basis for TMUV host adaptation and provide insights into flavivirus mosquito-to-waterfowl transmission.

Journal of Virology.title: The reovirus σ3 protein induces proteasomal degradation of IKKβ to modulate the host response to infection.
Journal of Virology.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Reovirus strains differ in their capacity to modulate host antiviral signaling, but the viral factors that control these differences have remained unclear. In this study, we identify outer capsid protein σ3 as the viral determinant responsible for inducing the loss of the NF-κB kinase components, IKKβ and NEMO. We demonstrate that the introduction of the σ3-encoding gene segment of strain T3A in the background of strain T3DL recapitulates IKK loss observed during T3A infection. Our results indicate that de novo expression of T3A σ3 during infection is necessary to mediate the loss of IKK. Further, the presence of T3A σ3 alone is sufficient. We show that T3A σ3 interacts with the IKK complex and targets IKKβ for degradation through a Cullin-RING ligase-proteasome-dependent mechanism. Loss of IKKβ results in impaired NF-κB activation and reduced IFN-β expression. Consequently, the T3DL/T3A S4 monoreassortant exhibits a replication advantage compared to T3DL. Collectively, these findings uncover a previously uncharacterized mechanism by which reovirus σ3 suppresses innate antiviral signaling through targeted degradation of IKKβ, providing new insight into reovirus-mediated immune modulation. [IMPORTANCE] Successful viral infection and replication require that the virus suppress host immune defenses, particularly innate immunity, which relies on signaling cascades to produce antiviral cytokines. Many viruses encode proteins to target key signaling molecules, such as those in the NF-κB pathway, but the exact mechanisms of evasion vary across viral families and even between closely related strains. In this study, we uncover a novel function of the reovirus outer capsid protein σ3 in promoting the degradation of the IKK complex, a regulator of NF-κB. Our findings reveal that σ3 associates with IKKβ to mediate its degradation via the proteasomal pathway. σ3-mediated loss of IKK decreases type I IFN expression during infection and enhances viral replication. Coupled with previous observations that σ3 from other reovirus strains antagonizes NF-κB by altering its transcriptional activity, this work demonstrates that this conserved viral protein adopts strain-specific strategies to subvert host defenses.

mBio.title: Characterizing malaria parasite drug response using single-cell transcriptomics.
mBio.abstract: Gene expression analysis in malaria parasites has been used to define transcriptional regulatory networks but has been used less frequently to characterize parasite response to drug treatment or to show how parasites may evade killing. Here, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to hundreds of thousands of individually infected asynchronous red blood cells to evaluate the parasite's response to treatment with three chemotypes that can be used for treatment (artemisinin) or prophylaxis and treatment (atovaquone and ganaplacide). We found that each treatment gave rise to different cell populations with different transcriptional profiles. Comparing single-cell transcription patterns in compound-treated cells to transcript patterns observed previously with synchronized cells showed an enrichment of cells expressing gametocyte-associated genes after artemisinin treatment but fewer life cycle perturbations after treatment with the two other compounds. In contrast, bulk analysis showed an enrichment of pyrimidine biosynthesis transcripts for atovaquone treatment. Our results show that scRNA-seq may be used to profile diverse drug responses across many life cycle stages and to potentially classify drug classes.IMPORTANCEDetermining the mechanism of action (MOA) of compounds with antimalarial activity remains a key activity in both drug development and drug resistance studies but remains challenging for some chemotypes. Here we highlight the potential of single-cell transcriptional sequencing to augment the process of MOA deconvolution. We develop a new analytical pipeline that involves comparing single-cell transcription patterns to existing profiles from synchronized parasites to comprehensively characterize life cycle stage enrichments that may be observed after chemical perturbations. We also show that transcriptional feedback regulation may be present for some drug classes.

mBio.title: Japanese encephalitis virus infection reshapes the gut microbiome and induces colonic inflammation in neonatal mice.
mBio.abstract: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), a neurotropic flavivirus, predominantly causes severe infection in children, leading to neuropsychiatric complications. Given that the juvenile period is a transitional window for the gut microbiota to develop into a stable community profile, any alterations to the microbiota during infections can result in chronic inflammation. Therefore, we investigated changes in the gut microbiota of neonatal mice during the early and late stages of JEV infection. Postnatal day 10, BALB/c mice challenged with JEV succumbed to acute infection at 6 to 7 days post-infection. This severity was marked by a surge in systemic pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-6, and MCP-1) and reduced food intake. Fecal 16S rRNA V3-V4 sequencing revealed distinct β-diversity between mock and JEV-infected groups, with the dominant phyla being Firmicutes, Bacteroidota, and Proteobacteria. The relative abundance of these phyla shifted, with Firmicutes decreasing from ~63.7% (control) to ~39% (JEV), whereas Proteobacteria remained unchanged in JEV. The Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio decreased in JEV, along with a reduction in Lactobacillus. Simultaneously, altered mucosal secretion, reduced tight-junction protein ZO-1, increased pNF-κB, and cleaved caspase-3 together indicated colonic inflammation. Prediction of microbial pathways using PICRUSt2 suggested a reduction in specific pathways associated with beneficial secondary metabolites and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in JEV. Intragastric administration of the SCFA cocktail prolonged survival and delayed the onset of clinical signs and the inflammatory response. Our findings suggest that systemic inflammation and reduced feeding during an acute infection could result in colonic dysbiosis, reduced beneficial bacteria, and trigger inflammation. SCFAs displayed a transient therapeutic effect in JEV infection, highlighting the potential of gut microbiota modulation to manage acute viral infection.IMPORTANCEJapanese encephalitis remains a leading cause of viral encephalitis in children across the Asia-Pacific region, with new outbreaks driven by evolving demographic factors. The need for targeted therapies beyond existing supportive care underscores the need for new host-directed interventions. Our findings suggest that gut-brain axis interactions may play a role in acute viral infections, potentially amplifying disease severity through infection-driven reduction in feeding, increased cytokine production, and shifts in the gut microbiome. We propose that SCFA supplementation can serve as a microbiota-modulating strategy that offers a safe, translatable approach to managing inflammation and JEV outcomes in pediatric viral encephalitis. This could be utilized as a supplement along with supportive care in other flavivirus infections.

mBio.title: The ER protein CGAF1 stabilizes CDC50.1 and drives nascent guanylate cyclase complex assembly for apical trafficking in Toxoplasma gondii.
mBio.abstract: [UNLABELLED] The apicomplexan guanylate cyclase (GC) complex acts as a signaling hub linking environmental sensing to lytic growth via production of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP). In Toxoplasma gondii, at least three accessory proteins (CDC50.1, UGO, and SLF) form a complex with GC to regulate its trafficking and activity. To further resolve the assembly and composition of the GC complex in T. gondii, we screened for novel interactors of GC using proximity-dependent biotin identification (BioID). In addition to all known GC complex members, we identified a highly enriched hypothetical protein (TGGT1_294940) that is restricted to the Sarcocystidae family of tissue-cyst-forming apicomplexans. 294940 possesses an N-terminal signal peptide followed by a single transmembrane motif, an architecture reminiscent of resident endoplasmic reticulum (ER) type I membrane proteins. Super-resolution imaging and biochemical fractionation established 294940 as a resident ER membrane protein, distinguishing it from the mature GC complex, which localizes to the apical plasma membrane. Conditional depletion of 294940 delayed replication and substantially impaired egress in tachyzoites, ablating lytic growth. Analysis of the 294940 interactome by co-immunoprecipitation revealed GC and CDC50.1 as its top two interactors, while UGO and SLF were unexpectedly absent, suggesting that 294940 regulates an initial step of GC complex assembly in the ER. Loss of 294940 caused rapid degradation of the GC chaperone CDC50.1, preventing GC exit from the ER and subsequent apical trafficking. Collectively, these data support a model whereby 294940 drives nascent CDC50.1-GC complex assembly in the ER for trafficking to the apical plasma membrane. Thus, we propose naming 294940 CDC50.1-Guanylate Cyclase Assembly Factor 1 (CGAF1). [IMPORTANCE] Cyclic GMP signaling is essential for motility, egress, and host cell invasion in apicomplexan parasites, yet how the guanylate cyclase (GC) signaling complex is assembled and delivered to the parasite surface remains poorly understood. Our study identifies CGAF1 as a previously uncharacterized, ER-resident membrane protein required for GC complex biogenesis. We show that CGAF1 acts at an early assembly step, enabling GC to pair with its chaperone CDC50.1 in the ER; without CGAF1, CDC50.1 is degraded, and GC fails to traffic to the apical plasma membrane, resulting in defective cGMP-dependent egress. These findings identify the first dedicated assembly factor for a CDC50-P4-ATPase or CDC50-GC complex in any organism and reveal that Sarcocystidae parasites have evolved a unique strategy, or quality checkpoint, for assembling these complexes. Understanding how apicomplexans build and deploy their GC signaling machinery offers new insight into the molecular basis of parasite egress and may point to lineage-specific vulnerabilities for therapeutic intervention.

EMBO Reports.title: Single-cell profiling of bam mutant germaria identifies gcrf1 as a regulator of TOR signaling in GSC.
EMBO Reports.abstract: In the Drosophila ovary, germline stem cells (GSCs) sustain oogenesis through a tightly regulated balance between self-renewal and differentiation. Although bag of marbles (bam) mutant ovaries have long been considered to predominantly consist of homogeneous GSC-like cells, the developmental states and regulatory programs underlying these undifferentiated germ cells remain poorly understood. Here, single-cell profiling of bam mutant ovaries uncovers distinct germ cell states, including two undifferentiated populations distinguished by eggpl expression and morphological features of bam mutant ovarioles. Comparative analyses further identify potential regulatory networks that are active at discrete developmental stages and reveal gcrf1 as a previously uncharacterized GSC-enriched gene. Functional studies demonstrate that gcrf1 promotes TORC1 signaling in early germ cells by activating the Rheb-S6K-S6 phosphorylation axis. Together, our findings reveal the developmental landscape of tumorigenesis caused by GSC differentiation defects and identify gcrf1 as a nutrient-responsive regulator linking TORC1 signaling to GSC maintenance.

FEMS Microbiology Reviews.title: Microbial adhesion to solid surfaces - the concept of preferential binding.
FEMS Microbiology Reviews.abstract: Microbial adhesion is the process by which individual microorganisms attach to a surface. It is a key process for microbial life: adhesion allows to colonize ecological niches, but also to interact with other organisms in symbiotic or pathogenic relationships. While we understand the importance of adhesion in microbial life in general, the underlying molecular mechanisms are less clear. Molecular details of adhesion processes have been elucidated only for some individual examples, mostly for human pathogens in the context of infections. In this review, we focus on the adhesion to non-living, solid surfaces, and summarize the limited understanding of the molecular principles of these interactions. We describe how proteins and other biomolecules interact with surfaces, and how microbes, and specifically bacteria, employ these interactions to enable a sessile lifestyle. We introduce the concept of preferential binding that describes specificity, affinity, and cooperativity of microbial adhesins and their interactions with different materials and surfaces. This concept more accurately describes the binding affinity to different surfaces, compared to the current textbook terminology coined for the interactions of enzymes or protein complexes. A molecular understanding of these processes, using concepts and methods across all disciplines of natural sciences, is key to the development of new disinfection and antifouling strategies that are in high demand in the post-antibiotic era.

PLOS Computational Biology.title: Neuronal XOR computation requires temporally activated synaptic information
PLOS Computational Biology.abstract: by Yanheng Li, Xiaojuan Sun, Yunliang Zang Single neurons can perform complex exclusive-or (XOR) computation which is conventionally thought to need multilayer networks, yet the biophysical mechanisms and the robustness of such computations under stochastic synaptic drive remain unclear. Using biologically realistic modeling, we demonstrate that dendritic depolarization block provides a universal and robust mechanism for XOR-like computation. Voltage-gated calcium channels enable a non-monotonic input-output relationship: moderate asynchronous drive evokes spiking, whereas excessive drive induces a sustained plateau that suppresses output, naturally implementing XOR logic computation. This computation is strictly gated by temporal distribution of synaptic inputs rather than spatial distribution; the XOR-like response is robust across diverse dendritic configurations but collapses under synchronous activation. Dendritic depolarization block propagates to the soma via dendrite-soma coupling, establishing a neuronal output-limiting mechanism. The computation is highly efficient, leveraging a frequency–synapse-count trade-off to ensure stable logic operations across varying levels of background activity. Cross-morphological validation confirms that XOR-like computation is morphology-independent, representing a generalizable biophysical principle of neural information processing.

PLOS Computational Biology.title: Epidemic control under incomplete observations through mechanistic state reconstruction and multi-agent learning
PLOS Computational Biology.abstract: by Shang Wang, Yuxiao Luo, Yunduan Cui, Meng Zhang, Min Kang, Ling Yin Epidemic-control policies are usually optimized from reported infection states, but these reports are often incomplete because testing capacity, reporting behavior, delays, and asymptomatic infections vary across regions and time. Such observation gaps can distort the state used by the controller and lead to suboptimal testing and isolation decisions. We develop a three-stage computational epidemiology framework that links observation modeling, state reconstruction, and policy optimization. First, we extend a metapopulation SEIQR model to represent fully observable, steady partially observable, and non-steady partially observable surveillance regimes. Second, we introduce ODE-DynNet, a hybrid reconstruction model that combines mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics with graph-temporal learning to infer hidden infection states from distorted observations. Third, we formulate coordinated testing and isolation as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem with a flow-based responsibility-aware reward that attributes transmission costs across connected regions. Using community-level mobility data from Shenzhen, China, we show that ODE-DynNet reduces infection cost by 88% (from 4,930 to 590) relative to the non-steady partially observable, decoupled policy that uses the raw proxy without reconstruction. The same pipeline remains effective across transmission intensities and reporting-delay settings, indicating that explicit observation modeling and state reconstruction are useful preprocessing steps for learned epidemic-control policies under incomplete surveillance.

PLOS Computational Biology.title: A flexible agent-based modelling framework of multi-serotype pneumococcal carriage to evaluate vaccine strategies in large populations
PLOS Computational Biology.abstract: by Nefel Tellioglu, David J. Price, Xinghui Chen, Violeta Spirkoska, Cyan Yingying Wang, Robert Moss, Natalie Carvalho, Kylie S. Carville, Patricia Therese Campbell, Jodie McVernon Streptococcus pneumoniae is a multi-serotype pathogen causing a substantial global burden of pneumonia and invasive bacterial disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been implemented worldwide, protecting against colonisation and disease from selected high-burden serotypes, but in many settings short-term effectiveness has been eroded by serotype replacement. Vaccines with broader serotype coverage have been developed, at the cost of immunogenicity against single serotypes. To determine the longer-term impact of these new formulations, we propose a novel modelling framework that evaluates the relationship between serotype-specific vaccine immunogenicity and effectiveness, comprising immunity, carriage and clinical models. Dynamics of individual serotypes are modelled over time, advancing existing modelling paradigms that group all serotypes according to vaccine type. This framework is sufficiently flexible to consider diverse populations, emerging vaccine formulations and implementation strategies. A retrospective analysis of sequential introduction of 7- and 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccines in Australia demonstrates the flexibility of the model.

PLOS Computational Biology.title: Robust parametric estimation of avian cranial morphology
PLOS Computational Biology.abstract: by Kaikwan Lau, Gary P. T. Choi Quantifying morphology from 3D scans is increasingly central to comparative biology, yet many existing pipelines require labor-intensive manual landmarking and impose strict assumptions on the data quality, hindering the high-throughput analysis of large and often imperfect digitized collections. In this work, we develop a fully unsupervised geometric framework that extracts robust parametric descriptors of cranial morphology directly from imperfect 3D skull meshes. Specifically, utilizing tools in computational geometry, differential geometry, and numerical optimization, the framework automatically aligns each specimen, measures the primary skull dimensions, and fits geometric primitives to the orbit and the neurocranium via robust iterative schemes, yielding stable estimates even for topologically noisy or damaged meshes. We demonstrate the framework on 100 skull specimens of Darwin’s finches and their relatives. The extracted measurements recover the well-established scaling relationship between skull size and orbit curvature, providing a biological validation of the automated pipeline. Building on this, we establish a predictive model that estimates the orbit curvature from three easily obtainable linear skull measurements, explaining 86.36% of the variance in curvature with an average prediction error of only 6.14%, and further derive dimensionless relative-geometry descriptors that are invariant to uniform scaling and retain variation among the sampled genera. We also demonstrate the generalizability of our method by applying it to other avian and mammalian skulls. Altogether, our work establishes a rigorous foundation for the digital estimation and high-throughput phenotyping of large-scale museum collections without the need for manual landmarking.

PLOS Computational Biology.title: Ten simple rules for creating and maintaining FAIR competency frameworks
PLOS Computational Biology.abstract: by Denise Bianco, Daria Sokolova, Matthew Forshaw, Clementina Ramirez Marengo, Emma Karoune, Kim T. Gurwitz, Vera Matser In a modern skills-based economy, competency frameworks are essential tools for workforce planning, career progression, and professional development. However, traditional frameworks often exist as static, isolated documents that lack digital connectivity and machine-readability. This article introduces a strategic roadmap to modernise professional standards by applying the FAIR principles: making competency frameworks Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. We present the FAIR competency framework lifecycle, an iterative model centred on end-user engagement, and outline 10 simple rules to guide creators through every stage of development. These rules cover foundational definitions, clear language, persistent identifiers, permissive licensing, and robust governance. By turning frameworks into machine-actionable digital objects, organisations can ensure their standards are easily discoverable, reusable, and ready to integrate into broader learning management systems. Ultimately, adopting these guidelines promotes a more interconnected, transparent, and adaptable global skills landscape where professional expertise can be recognised and shared efficiently.

Water Research.title: The performance of one-stage PNA process coupled with nitrate removal-targeted electrochemical unit.
Water Research.abstract: During the operation of the one-stage partial nitritation/anammox (PNA) process, nitrate is the inevitable product, which not only limits the total nitrogen removal efficiency (NRE), but also brings the burden of post-denitrification treatment. Electrochemical nitrate reduction is a potentially effective route for nitrate removal with merits such as no second pollution and sludge production. Therefore, in this study, for the first time, a one-stage PNA-electrochemical (EC) unit system, with Cu(I)/Cu(II) oxide nanowires as the cathode for nitrate removal and IrO₂-Ta₂O₅/Ti mesh as the anode, was developed. The results showed that the EC unit worked well with PNA process under proper condition, finally NRE of the whole system reached 84.1 ± 2.0%, and the effluent nitrate concentration was markedly lower than the theoretical value with the maximum nitrate reduction efficiency reached 45.8%. Moreover, the electroactive denitrifiers (Denitratisoma and Brevundimonas) and the hydrogenotrophic denitrifier (Hydrogenophaga) were detected in the system. Both theoretical analysis and separate batch experiments indicated that nitrate was mainly converted into nitrite attributed to the electrochemical nitrate reduction and the hydrogenotrophic denitrification. Notably the external aeration demand decreased by approximately 41%, which was likely attributed to the oxygen released from anodic oxygen evolution reaction. These findings together indicate a synergistic interaction between the biological process and electrochemical process. Overall, coupling one-stage PNA with EC unit is promising in enabling the effective removal of nitrate produced during the PNA process and potentially paving the way to overcome the NRE limit of PNA process. This novel process also gives a reference for addressing the intrinsic limitation of other anammox-based processes.

Applied and Environmental Microbiology.abstract: It has been demonstrated that 2',3'-cGMP modulates the physiology of Ralstonia solanacearum by inhibiting the regulatory activity of the transcriptional regulator RSp0980. Here, we report that 2',3'-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2',3'-cNMPs), including 2',3'-cAMP, 2',3'-cGMP, 2',3'-cCMP, and 2',3'-cUMP, which are synthesized by the RNase T1 homolog RSc2766, play a critical role in the modulation of R. solanacearum virulence through another receptor. 2',3'-cNMPs specifically bind to the LysR-type transcriptional regulator RSc2761 and thus increase the regulatory activity of RSc2761 on the transcription of target genes. Intriguingly, the 2',3'-cNMP-RSc2761 signaling system also regulates the transcription of phcA, which encodes the master regulator of the quorum-sensing (QS) network, and subsequently controls the production of QS signals and virulence in R. solanacearum. Together, our work provides new insights into the regulatory mechanisms of 2',3'-cNMPs through multiple signaling pathways, suggesting that R. solanacearum utilizes a complex and precise signaling network to control its pathogenicity.IMPORTANCERalstonia solanacearum is a plant pathogen that causes destructive bacterial wilt and leads to severe crop losses worldwide. This study deciphers the synthetic pathway of the intracellular second messengers 2',3'-cNMPs in R. solanacearum. In addition, we demonstrate that 2',3'-cNMPs specifically act on the transcriptional regulator RSc2761, which in turn controls the pathogenicity of R. solanacearum by regulating the transcription of phcA and other target genes. Our findings unveil a novel 2',3'-cNMP-mediated pathogenicity regulatory pathway in R. solanacearum and provide potential targets for the control of bacterial wilt disease.

Genome Biology.title: Human astrocyte aging couples chromatin closure to focal G-quadruplex accumulation
Genome Biology.abstract: Background Aging disrupts genome organization and transcriptional fidelity, but the role of non-canonical DNA structures remains unclear. G-quadruplexes (G4s) are stable, guanine-rich DNA and RNA structures that regulate gene expression and genome integrity. However, their contribution to aging remains unknown. Here, we examine age-associated changes in G4 abundance, chromatin accessibility, and G4-helicase DDX5 expression in human astrocytes established from the brain resections of donors spanning early to late adulthood and expanded in culture before analysis. Results Imaging with N-TASQ and BG4 shows increased G4 signal in astrocytes from older donors, together with reduced nuclear DDX5 expression. ATAC-seq profiling reveals an age-associated decline in chromatin accessibilityat intergenic, intronic, and promoter-proximal regions. Genome-wide mapping of G4s by G4 CUT&Tag identifies focal enrichment at specific loci in older astrocytes, including sites within both accessible and less accessible chromatin. We overexpress DDX5 in young astrocytes and observe transcriptional changes in pathways associated with chromatin organization, genome maintenance, stress signaling, and synaptic function. In contrast, acute DDX5 depletion causes focal G4 accumulation without reproducing broader chromatin changes observed with aging. Conclusions This study defines an age-associated axis in human astrocytes that links reduced DDX5, focal G4 abundance, and progressive loss of chromatin accessibility. Our findings identify G4 regulation as a candidate mechanism shaping genome control during astrocyte aging.

Briefings in Bioinformatics.title: Transformer models in genomics: from sequence analysis to population genetics and biodiversity
Briefings in Bioinformatics.abstract: AbstractModern genomics and artificial intelligence converge at a breakthrough point with the emergence of transformer-based large language models for genomic analysis. This review examines how transformer-based models have advanced genomic sequence analysis through novel tokenization strategies, self-attention mechanisms, and pre-training/fine-tuning paradigms. Unlike prior broad surveys, we focus on three sub-areas of genomics where transformer architectures have had a substantive impact: sequence-level analysis, population-level genetics, including genetic imputation and genome-wide association analysis, and biodiversity research, while addressing challenges like genome-scale computational demands, training biases, and interpreting attention in biological contexts. Looking forward, we outline how emerging foundation models, multi-modal integration, and biologically informed attention mechanisms could transform our understanding of genome function, providing a roadmap for leveraging genome language models to decode genome complexity and advance functional and population-level genomics.

Briefings in Bioinformatics.title: CN-RNN: a deep learning framework for copy number variants detection with exome sequencing data
Briefings in Bioinformatics.abstract: AbstractCopy number variations (CNVs) are major structural genomic variants that contribute to a wide range of human diseases. Accurate CNV detection from whole-exome sequencing (WES) data remains challenging because existing callers often exhibit high false-positive rates and limited sensitivity for short CNVs. Moreover, current deep learning approaches do not fully integrate the complementary information provided by local read-depth patterns and region-level genomic features. Here we present CN-RNN, a two-stage framework that combines high-sensitivity candidate generation with deep learning-based candidate classification. The framework integrates a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) branch, which captures local depth changes and contextual dependencies across neighboring exons, with a parallel multi-layer perceptron (MLP) branch that incorporates region-level features including GC content, mappability, and exon length. The model was trained using parent-offspring trios from the Autism Sequencing Consortium (ASC), with training labels constructed through Mendelian inheritance filtering. In internal validation and evaluation with two independent external datasets constructed using distinct reference sets, CN-RNN consistently outperformed existing WES-based CNV callers and deep learning methods. These results demonstrate that integrating sequential read-depth patterns with region-level genomic features improves the accuracy and generalizability of CNV detection from WES data. CN-RNN provides a scalable tool for CNV profiling in population and clinical sequencing studies and is available at https://github.com/FeifeiXiao-lab/CN-RNN.

Journal of Evolutionary Biology.title: Out of the cradle: secondary expansion from a source lake is associated with loss of morphological distinctiveness in endemic Kamchatkan charrs (Salvelinus).
Journal of Evolutionary Biology.abstract: The contribution of postglacial adaptive radiations to regional freshwater fish biodiversity remains debated. To test whether such radiations can give rise to new populations in neighboring ecosystems, we reconstructed the evolutionary history of the endemic Salvelinus malma assemblage of Lake Kronotskoe (Kamchatka). We traced the dispersal of endemic lineages from the lake into adjacent basins and quantified morphological divergence between lacustrine charrs and their derived populations. Using SNPs from SLAF-seq loci, we analyzed phylogeny, genetic differentiation, contemporary hybridization and historical gene flow among eleven charr groups, and complemented these analyses with morphometric comparisons. Our results indicate that the lacustrine-addfluvial predatory and benthivorous lineages of the Lake Kronotskoe basin colonized small peripheral waterbodies via temporary riverbed connections during the Holocene. These lineages also continue to disperse downstream from the lake, which is isolated by rapids, and hybridize with anadromous S. malma. These migrations have given rise to three new isolated populations and one hybrid anadromous population. Morphological evolution in the derived populations was independent of their phylogenetic history and converged on a generalized morphology typical of pelagic or riverine fish. Thus, postglacial expansion of adaptive morphs from the source lake enhances regional diversity, while migrants can rapidly lose ancestral adaptive traits in new habitats.

Trends in Ecology & Evolution.title: Characterizing wildlife’s behavioral response to humans
authors: Kenta Uchida, Daniel T. Blumstein, Masashi Soga
Trends in Ecology & Evolution.abstract: Human–wildlife interactions are critically important across biodiversity conservation, public health, and urban sustainability. Defining wildlife behavioral responses to humans is essential for managing these interactions, yet existing knowledge remains fragmented. We provide a framework to understand and predict behavioral responses to humans. We classify responses into four categories—avoidance, attraction, defense, and unresponsive—that generate diverse ecological and societal consequences. The prevalence of these response types varies across spatial and temporal scales in context-dependent ways because animals adjust their perceived risk–reward balance in response to humans, as well as nonhuman ecological, internal, and abiotic factors. By providing a common framework to explain this variation, we highlight opportunities to improve the prediction and management of human–wildlife relationships in a human-dominated world.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: Unraveling sodium and lithium stress phenotypes in a Bacillus safensis strain isolated from Chilika Lake by ATR-FTIR chemometrics.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] The increasing use of lithium-ion batteries has heightened interest in microbial responses to lithium-bearing waste streams, yet bacterial responses to LiCl remain poorly resolved. A lithium-tolerant strain from Chilika Lake, India, was isolated and confirmed as Bacillus safensis by 16S rRNA and multilocus phylogeny. Both maximum tolerable concentration (MTC) conditions supported sustained growth under 1.8 M NaCl and 1.5 M LiCl, although LiCl produced a lower apparent specific growth rate and longer generation time. Whole-cell attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) spectra were examined and subsequently analyzed for 120 cultures representing control, single-salt, and combined-salt treatments. In the 900-1,800 cm-1 fingerprint region, Savitzky-Golay smoothing, followed by vector normalization, yielded the most stable pre-processing workflow. The final partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) model showed strong nested cross-validated discrimination (balanced accuracy, 0.875 ± 0.068; macro-F1, 0.866 ± 0.068; macro-area under the ROC curve [AUC], 0.964 ± 0.011), and nested permutation testing confirmed non-random separation (P = 0.0062). High-variable importance in projection (VIP) features were concentrated in carbohydrate/phosphate- and amide-associated regions, including a high-frequency amide I feature at 1,682.4 cm-1. Residual soluble protein in dialyzed 48-h culture supernatants showed a non-monotonic response under single-salt exposure but progressive depletion across the combined NaCl and LiCl gradient. These findings establish reproducible treatment-associated biochemical states and support ATR-FTIR chemometrics as a phenotypic approach for microbial ionic-stress analysis, while recognizing that osmotic and ion-specific contributions require osmolality-controlled validation. [IMPORTANCE] This work shows how an environmental bacterium may respond to a stress associated with lithium. As lithium-ion batteries become more common, lithium-containing waste is increasing, and little is known about how aquatic microbes respond to lithium exposure. By studying a bacterium isolated from Chilika Lake, the research shows that sodium, lithium, and their combination affect bacterial cells differently. Using a rapid biochemical fingerprinting method, the study detected changes in the overall cellular chemistry under different stress-associated conditions. It also found that combined sodium and lithium stress changes the surrounding soluble protein environment differently from single-salt stress. These findings matter because microbes are essential for aquatic ecosystem functioning, and understanding their response to lithium may help predict environmental impacts and support future eco-friendly lithium management strategies.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: Molecular epidemiology of the Taiwan (GI-7) IBV genotype in China over six decades: uncovering recombination hotspots and a nationwide transmission network.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a Gammacoronavirus, challenges the poultry industry through high mutation and recombination rates. The Taiwan (GI-7) genotype has become dominant in China, yet its evolutionary origins and spread remain unclear. We analyzed 196 Taiwan (GI-7) IBV isolates collected over 60 years, focusing on the S1 gene, which contains three hypervariable regions (HVRs) critical for antigenicity, receptor binding, and serotype specificity, using phylogenetic, recombination, evolutionary, and phylogeographic methods. The isolates split into two subgroups, Taiwan-I (dominant) and Taiwan-II, with increasing prevalence since 2011. Recombination analysis detected events in 33 isolates, with breakpoints at nucleotides 1,096 (HVR III), 1,263, and 1,467. Two positively selected sites were identified: codon 39 (Gly) in HVR I and codon 121 (Gly/Ala) in HVR II, both located in the receptor-binding domain. The S1 gene evolved at 1.644 × 10-3 substitutions/site/year, originating in the early 1950s in Taiwan. Phylogeography revealed spread from Taiwan to Guangxi, then throughout China and Japan. Bayesian skyline analysis showed rapid population growth after 2006. This study clarifies the origins, transmission routes, and evolution of Taiwan (GI-7) IBV, providing a basis for improved surveillance and control. [IMPORTANCE] Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) poses a persistent threat to global poultry health and productivity. This study elucidates the evolutionary history and transmission network of the dominant Taiwan (GI-7) IBV genotype in China. By integrating genomic and phylodynamic analyses, we identify key recombination hotspots in the S1 gene and trace the origin of this genotype to Taiwan, revealing its rapid spread across China and East Asia since the 1950s. These findings highlight the role of recombination and positive selection in shaping viral diversity and dominance. Our work provides a critical foundation for targeted surveillance and control strategies to mitigate the impact of IBV on poultry production systems.

eLife.title: Endocardial TIE1 synergizes with TIE2 to regulate the atrial internal muscular network assembly
eLife.abstract: Atrial cardiomyopathy is characterized by altered atrial structures, yet its underlying genetic basis remains inadequately explored. TIE1 mutations are reported in lymphedema patients, but whether they exhibit cardiac defects alongside lymphatic abnormalities remains unknown. Here, single-cell RNA sequencing showed high Tie1 and Tek expression in atrial endocardial cells. TIE1 deficiency severely disrupted atrial morphogenesis, with only minor ventricular defects. Bulk RNA-seq showed reduced transcripts for endothelial development and cardiac trabeculation in Tie1 mutants. Separate RNA-seq analysis of the atria and ventricles further confirmed these findings, revealing a more pronounced downregulation of trabecular genes, including Tek, in the atria upon Tie1 loss. Endothelial deletion of Tek impaired trabeculation, particularly in atria. Consistently, Tie1 loss combined with a single null Tek allele disrupted both atrial and ventricular trabeculation. Strikingly, atrial morphogenesis defects appeared within 48 hr of induced endothelial Tie1 loss coupled with Tek heterozygous deletion, implying a critical endocardial role in organizing the atrial muscular network. The synergy of TIE1 and TIE2 in remodeling atrial trabeculae was confirmed postnatally, whereas TIE1 insufficiency alone had no obvious effect. Together, TIE1 is differentially required for atrial versus ventricular development, acting synergistically with TIE2 to regulate endocardial cell-coordinated assembly of atrial internal muscular network.

PLOS Biology.title: Allosteric inhibition rescues hydrocephalus caused by catalytically inactive Shp2 in mice
PLOS Biology.abstract: by Neoklis Makrides, Emily Sun, Hilal Mir, Jen-Zen Chuang, Ziyuan Jiang, Yihua Wu, Carlos Serra, John Peregrin, Qian Wang, Wellington V. Cardoso, Ching-Hwa Sung, Neel H. Shah, Xin Zhang SHP2, a protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) crucial in Ras-MAPK signaling, is associated with various human congenital diseases and cancers. Here, we show that the catalytically inactive Shp2C459S mutation results in communicating hydrocephalus, similar to the catalytically activating Shp2E76K and Mek1DD mutants. Unlike previous mutants, however, Shp2C459S/+ mutation uniquely affects ciliary development rather than neurogenesis, leading to structural abnormalities in cilia and impaired ciliary motility. Differential scanning fluorimetry suggested that SHP2C459S, SHP2E76K, and SHP2C459S/E76K mutations all induce an open SHP2 conformation, but only SHP2C459S leads to aberrant GAB1 phosphorylation in cells expressing wild-type SHP2. Consistent with this distinct signaling profile, brain ventricular tissues from Shp2C459S/+ mice exhibit elevated GAB1 and AKT phosphorylation despite normal ERK and STAT3 activities, implicating dysregulated PI3K–AKT signaling in the pathogenesis of hydrocephalus. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K markedly rescues ciliogenesis defects and alleviates hydrocephalus in mutant mice. Furthermore, the allosteric SHP2 inhibitor SHP099 increases the thermal stability of SHP2C459S protein, consistent with a shift toward a closed state, and ameliorates hydrocephalus in Shp2C459S/+ mice. These findings suggest that, in this engineered mouse model, Shp2-associated hydrocephalus is driven by conformational changes rather than altered catalytic activity. Our results underscore the therapeutic potential of conformation-specific allosteric inhibitors in targeting both catalytically active and inactive SHP2 mutants.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Endocrine-Disrupting Effects and Reproductive Toxicity of Metal-Based Nanoparticles through DRP1-Mediated Mitophagy within an Adverse Outcome Pathway Framework.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The widespread use of metal-based nanoparticles (NPs), including Ag, ZnO, and TiO2 NPs, in industrial and consumer products has raised concerns about their potential endocrine-disrupting effects and reproductive toxicity. Conventional safety assessment approaches may not adequately capture the complex mechanisms underlying NP-induced toxicity. To our knowledge, this study is the first to integrate OECD-recommended assays, high-throughput screening, an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) framework, and the Toxicological Prioritization Index (ToxPi) to investigate the endocrine-disrupting effects and reproductive toxicity of metal-based NPs. The results showed that ZnO and Ag NPs increased estrogen receptor (ER) transcriptional activity, whereas TiO2 NPs inhibited it. All NPs increased 17β-estradiol production, while ZnO and TiO2 NPs reduced testosterone production. ZnO NPs induced the generation of reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial dysfunction, and DRP1 activation, which were associated with subsequent apoptosis, mitophagy, and autophagy. In contrast, Ag NPs did not induce apoptosis or autophagy, suggesting distinct cytotoxic mechanisms. TiO2 NPs caused no significant cell death in MLTC-1 cells, even at high concentrations. ToxPi ranked COOH-ZnO NPs as the most toxic, followed by NH2-ZnO NPs, Ag NPs, and TiO2 NPs. This integrated framework could provide a practical approach for toxicity screening, mechanistic investigation, and hazard prioritization of NPs.

mSphere.title: Genome-wide synthetic engineering identifies essential genes and host-specific factors governing tropism switching in mycobacteriophage D29.
mSphere.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Mycobacteriophage D29 is a phage that infects mycobacteria and has been studied as a model since its isolation in 1954. It can infect multiple species, including Mycobacterium smegmatis, nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of tuberculosis. D29 is now considered a potential candidate for NTM and tuberculosis treatment. However, 34% of its genes remain functionally uncharacterized. Recent advances in synthetic biology have enabled efficient phage engineering, reducing the challenges of mutant screening in bulk populations. In this study, we generated a set of single-gene deletion mutants using synthetic engineering techniques to identify genes required for phage propagation. Functional analysis of all 77 genes showed that 44 genes (57%) and all tRNAs were nonessential for phage replication. Furthermore, infection assays using the deletion mutants demonstrated that genes 55, 56, and 59 are required for efficient infection of M. tuberculosis H37Rv but are dispensable for infection of M. smegmatis, highlighting their contribution to host-specific phage infectivity. These findings provide valuable insights into D29 biology and phage-host dynamics. [IMPORTANCE] In this study, we employed synthetic biology techniques to construct a comprehensive library of the gene and tRNA deletion mutants of mycobacteriophage D29 to systematically assess gene essentiality. Notably, over half of the genes were found to be nonessential for the lytic cycle, suggesting potential roles in environmental adaptation and host-mycobacteria interactions. Furthermore, we found that the D29Δ55, D29Δ56, and D29Δ59 mutants showed markedly reduced plating efficiency on Mycobacterium tuberculosis although these genes were dispensable for infection of Mycobacterium smegmatis. Such differential genetic requirements highlight their potential roles in modulating phage-host interactions across distinct Mycobacterium species. These findings provide valuable insights into the functional genomics of D29 and phage biology and support its continued development as a candidate for phage-based therapies against nontuberculous mycobacteria and M. tuberculosis infections.
